name: Week 31 Push — Dips Move Up, the Press Keeps the Front
description:
**The press stays first and gets the spotlight.** It ran from the front for the first time last week and produced three pure strict sets at 50 — no leg drive anywhere. That is the lift running on a full tank, and it now gets the deep cues to match.

**Dips move to second, and that is this week's experiment.** They ran early in W29 and produced the best set of the block; they ran last in W30 and were "a struggle after all those other exercises." Same load, same reps, opposite reports — which is the same lesson the press already taught. So dips get a fresh tank too.

**The tricep extension goes to 70.** Four weeks at 60 and last week it "never got hard."

**Incline holds 60 at the 3s eccentric, and the lateral raise holds 20.** Both already have their form lever pulled.

dayOverview.theme: Two lifts get the front of the session and everything else holds. The press keeps the slot that fixed it and gets the deep cues; dips take the slot behind it to find out whether their swing between best-of-the-block and struggle is about the lift or about the queue. One load moves — the tricep extension — because it stopped costing anything.

spotlights.why: A month of running it last, then one week running it first, and it went from unable to strict rep one of set two to three clean strict sets at 50. The slot is settled; now the lift itself is worth running deliberately.
Best set of the block when it ran early, a struggle when it ran late, same bodyweight both times. This week it runs second, and the question is whether the difference was ever the lift.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W32 — chest press machine and the Kinesis lateral raise come back when the week stops being short. W33 — the cable block returns to spotlight at its new numbers.
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: strict DB press, dips, incline DB press, straight-arm pulldown, farmer carry. Effort here means the cue holding at a hard load; the ceiling is the rep the cue breaks.
🔥 near-failure last set OK: DB lateral raise, incline cable tricep extension. Isolation work where form holds at the limit.

**⭐ THE STRICT PRESS GOES FIRST. This is settled and does not get re-tested.** If a busy gym forces it late, write it off as a push press and use leg drive rather than discovering mid-set that you cannot strict it.
**Dips are second this week, not fifth.** If they still feel like a struggle from that slot, the answer is the lift and not the queue — say so, because that changes what happens to them next.
**Take the full 2 minutes on both the press and the dips.** It is what let the slow tempo survive all three sets.
**Pack DOWN, not up** on every pressing lift. Blades into the back pockets, neck long, traps quiet. A rep that needs a shrug is over.

**The lateral raise load is NOT moving, and that is not a hold — the lever already got pulled.** You have been running them slower and wider, and a longer lever makes the same 20 a heavier lift. **Progress by going wider, not heavier.**
**Carry: 60 if the hands feel good, 50 if you are ready to go home.** Your rule, written in. No straps either way.
**A new crackle showed up in the left shoulder on pull day.** Nothing here changes for it, but notice whether the press or the dips provoke anything on that side and say so.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Chest Opener + Protective Shrug
sets.notes: The whole block, every push day. Yuri's band work is the shoulder anchor — it is why the right shoulder has stayed quiet through a heavy pressing block, so it does not get skipped on a short morning.

exercises.notes: Small to large. Just moving blood.
**The shoulder anchor.** Full sequence, light band, no rushing. Cuff first, then scap. **Take an extra beat on the left this week** — that is the side that got noisy on the bar.

Light bell, inverted. **Wrist stacked over elbow over shoulder** — the bell tipping is the feedback. It rehearses the exact packed-down lockout the press is about to ask for, and the press is the very next thing you do.
Light. This is the chest opener, not a working set.
Tight fists, thumbs tucked, hinged slightly forward. Wakes the deep core — the press needs the trunk before it needs the shoulders.
Elbows ~45°, **pack down not up.** One easy set.
Greasing set, nowhere near failure. Keeps the pattern alive on a push day.
**Protective activation — before anything loaded.** 40-50lb pair, behind the back, straight up and down.

sets.name: 🔆 Strict DB Press — 50, First Lift of the Day 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb pair, 3 sets of 6-8. **2 minutes between sets, reps as singles.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the slot is settled, so now the lift gets the attention.** Last week was the first time this ran on a full tank and it came back as three pure strict sets, no leg drive anywhere. The load is unchanged; what is worth watching is whether it is still genuinely strict on set 3 or whether a little knee creeps in when it gets hard.

**Setup:**
- **Bells to the shoulders, elbows slightly in front of the ribs**, not flared out to the sides
- **Feet about hip width, glutes and core braced** — you are the bench here, there is nothing behind you
- **Ribs DOWN before the first rep** and they stay down the whole set

**The press:**
- **No dip, no knee bend, no hip drive.** The set ends when strict form ends, not when the rep fails
- **Press slightly around the head, not straight up past the nose** — finish with the bells stacked over the shoulders and the biceps near the ears
- **Pack DOWN, not up.** If the shoulders climb toward the ears to finish a rep, that rep was the last one
- **Slow eccentric on every rep** — lower under control to the shoulders, do not let them drop

**Common faults:** leaning back to turn it into an incline press · ribs flaring open · a small knee dip sneaking in on the last two reps · the bells drifting forward of the shoulders at lockout.

**Reflection:** was set 3 still a *pure* strict press, or did a little leg sneak in to finish it?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb pair, 3 sets. 2 min rest, reps as singles.
- **Strict — no leg drive, no knee dip**
- **Slow eccentric every rep**
- Press slightly around the head; biceps near the ears at lockout
- Shoulders packed **DOWN**, traps relaxed, ribs down
- If the rack forces this late in the day, run it as a push press instead

sets.name: 🔆 Dips — Second This Week, 1s Pause at the Bottom 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** bodyweight, 3 sets of 10-12 on the **angled / V bar**. **2 minutes between sets — take all of it.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — this is a position test, not a load test.** In W29 dips ran early and gave you the best set of the block. In W30 they ran last and were "a struggle after all those other exercises." Nothing about the lift changed in between. **This week they run second, on a nearly full tank**, and the reflection below is the whole point of the move.

- **Rotate the left forearm outward before taking bodyweight** so the pressure sits on the firm inside edge of the hand, not the thumb pad
- Mini-dips against the bar to set the forward lean before rep 1
- **3s descent, then 1s still at the bottom** — shorten the set rather than rush either
- **Hold the forward lean** the whole set; drifting upright turns this into a triceps-only lift
- **Pack DOWN at lockout.** Shoulders climbing at the top is the set ending

**Reflection:** from the second slot, did these feel like W29's good day or W30's struggle? If they still struggled, the queue was never the problem.

exercises.notes:
Bodyweight, 3 sets. **Angled / V bar. 2 min rest.**
- Set the rotated palm position **before** the first rep
- **3s descent, 1s pause at the bottom**
- Hold the forward lean
- Shoulders packed down at lockout

sets.name: Incline DB Press — 60, 3s Eccentric Holds 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 60lb pair, 3 sets of 8-12. **3s eccentric, same as last week.** 2 minutes between sets.

The tempo bump got absorbed at an unchanged 60 and the last set was still "definitely working weight." Nothing moves.

- **Bench at 30°, not 45°**
- **3s eccentric on every rep** — this is the progression
- **Blades DOWN and BACK into the bench**, chest tall
- **Elbows around 45° from the torso**, not flared to 90
- Stop when the eccentric shortens or the shoulders shrug

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 60lb pair, all 3 sets.
- **30° bench**
- **3s eccentric every rep**
- Blades down and back, ribs down
- 2 min rest, reps as singles

sets.name: DB Lateral Raise — 20, Wider Is the Progression 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 20lb pair, 3 sets of 12-15.

**The load is not moving and the 25s are not coming.** You have been running these slower and with the bells held **wider** — farther from the body on a fixed slight elbow bend — and a longer lever makes the same 20 a heavier lift. That is the form lever, already pulled, and it is why last week was harder than the week before at an identical weight.

- **This week's progression line: a little wider than last week.** Not heavier
- **Slow up, slow down, 1s hold at the top**
- **Lead with the elbows**, little fingers a touch high
- **Traps quiet.** If the shoulders ride up to start the rep, the weight is winning
- Last set may run near failure — safe isolation work

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 20lb pair (15 if the 20s are taken — keep the width and tempo intact).
- **Wider than last week** is the progression
- Slow up / slow down / **1s hold**
- Lead with the elbow, fixed slight bend
- **Traps relaxed** — no shrug to start the rep

sets.name: Cable Block — Straight-Arm Pulldown → Lean-Back Tricep Pushdown (2 Rounds)
sets.notes:
**Two rounds, circuit style, minimal rest between the two moves.** Both live on the cable stations — take whichever is free and stay there.

**The extension steps to 70.** Four weeks at 60, and last week it ran with the cues followed and "never got hard." The pulldown holds at 120, which did bite at the end of both rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:**
- Cable column: **120**
- Rope pulley: **62.5**
- Kinesis: **6**
Pick whichever is free; **note the equipment and number in the log.**

- **Set a soft elbow bend and never change it** — if the elbow opens and closes, it has quietly become a triceps pushdown
- **Start the rep by pulling the upper arm down from the armpit**, not by pushing the hands
- Finish with the hands at the thighs, **lats squeezed, ribs down**
- **No leaning back to add range** — the torso angle is fixed too
- Slow return to a real stretch

**LOAD:** cable column **70**, up from 60. **60 is the fallback if the cues start slipping.**

- Torso leans back; hands travel from near the chest to straight arms **by the hips**
- **Elbows stay pinned in space — only the forearms move.** If the elbows drift forward on the way up, the lift has become a pushdown, and a heavier stack is exactly when that happens
- **Nothing goes behind the head** — that position is what the right arm dislikes
- **Pack the shoulders down before every set**, and keep them down as the arms straighten
- **Squeeze at full extension**, slow back
- If the right-arm nerve line returns and does not clear, stop the set

sets.name: Farmer Carry — 60 or 50, Your Call at the Handles 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD: 60lb per hand if the hands feel good, 50 if you are ready to go home.** 2 walks of ~50s. **No straps.**

That is your rule from last week, written in as the prescription. Both numbers are legitimate — pick at the handles, not in advance, and log which.

- **Crush the handles from the first step** rather than letting the grip fade into it
- **Shoulders packed down**, ribs stacked over hips, walk tall
- The job is two walks that both hold, not a heavier bell
- If the left goes early, set them down, rest, and finish the time

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 60 per hand, or 50. No straps. **Log which.**
- **Grip hard from the first step**
- Shoulders down, ribs stacked, tall posture
- Two walks that hold beats a heavier bell

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block
sets.notes: Five minutes, every gym day. Slow breathing throughout — the downshift is as much the point as the tissue.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm, elbow at MID height.
Passive. Let the shoulders decompress.
30s each side.
45s each side.
Slow breathing. End here.

tips: Press first, dips second. Both get the full 2 minutes between sets.
Dips are a position test this week — report whether the earlier slot changed them.
Lateral raise: wider, not heavier. The 25s are not the next step.
Tricep extension steps to 70; 60 is there if the elbows start drifting.
Carry is 60 or 50 by how the hands feel. Log which one you took.
